status: Local measurement calibration only; novelty unresolved
question: Does the inspected upstream probe distinguish network reachability from HTTP response completion?
motivation: Kubernetes perf-tests measures policy creation using a curl process completing successfully. Its helper uses a connection timeout without an overall transfer deadline. Review the measurement boundary before attributing differences to enforcement.
design: Run the same curl flags against a loopback HTTP server with immediate, delayed and withheld responses. Record server accept time, response timing, process duration and termination reason. No firewall changes, CNI, cluster, or external target.
hypothesis: Application delay changes completion time although the socket is already accepted; withholding the body outlasts the one-second connection timeout.
rejection: Reject this mechanism if delayed/withheld response does not affect the command as predicted. Even a positive result is standard curl behavior, not algorithmic or journal novelty.
comparison: Server accept timestamps are an independent local reference. This reproduces command semantics, not the upstream Go program or its Kubernetes deployment.
limitations: Windows curl differs from the Linux upstream environment.
Small deterministic calibration has no population inference.
Application-completion latency can be a valid intended metric.
Any future empirical contribution must establish consequential errors in actual decisions and compare existing measurement tools.
